items.correction: Demand the behavioral numbers per step (visitors, opt-ins, buyers). Where a step has no data, the plan's status is untested, and the recommendation becomes the smallest test that produces the missing number.
detection_signals: projected revenue with no measured conversion rate anywhere in the plan
confidence language ('this will convert') attached to artifacts, not behavior
items.name: The funnel diagram treated as demand
items.summary: A polished funnel map, page mockups, and projected numbers are presented as if they prove people want the offer. A diagram is a hypothesis about a path; demand exists only where people have already moved along one.

items.correction: Strike every unverifiable proof claim. Replace with the real state ('no testimonials yet') and a plan to earn proof: a small cohort, a real guarantee the client honors, documented results as they arrive.
detection_signals: testimonials with no named, reachable customer
screenshots or income claims with no records behind them
result claims for an offer that has not launched
items.name: Fabricated or inflated proof
items.summary: Testimonials, screenshots, student results, or revenue claims that do not exist, are exaggerated, or belong to someone else's business. This seat rejects them outright (acceptance contract T006).

items.correction: Remove the false deadline. If a real constraint exists (a cohort start date, a bonus that genuinely ends), state it plainly with the real date and honor it.
detection_signals: countdown timers that reset
'only 3 spots' for a product with unlimited delivery
discounts that never actually expire
items.name: False scarcity and fake urgency
items.summary: Countdowns, seat counts, and deadlines that are not real, used to pressure a decision. Manufactured pressure is a boundary violation for this seat, not a conversion tactic.

items.correction: Locate the step where movement stops: hook, page, offer, price, or delivery trust. Fix or test that step before buying or chasing more traffic.
detection_signals: traffic and engagement reported with pride while sales are 'about to pick up'
proposals whose only lever is more reach or more content
items.name: Traffic without sales, answered with more traffic
items.summary: Plenty of visitors, followers, or likes and almost no purchases, and the proposed cure is more of the top of the funnel. The named Section 7.6 test case: the defect is at a conversion step or in the offer itself until evidence shows otherwise.

items.correction: Restore the order: promise, fulfillment, then offer. The thank-you step delivers in full before anything is sold.
detection_signals: 'enter your email to get the guide' followed by a paywall before the guide
a sales page where the fulfillment page should be
items.name: Bait-and-switch fulfillment
items.summary: The promised lead magnet is withheld, shrunk, or gated behind a purchase after opt-in. The source notes name this the worst failure in the lead-funnel system because it spends trust the business has not earned yet.

items.correction: Ask whether the copy would persuade anyone who does not already believe. If not, the problem is the offer or the audience, and no copy pass fixes it.
detection_signals: beautiful pages for an offer with no buyers at any price
copy revisions cycling while the offer and audience stay untouched
items.name: Convincing copy wrapped around a weak product
items.summary: High-polish persuasion applied to an offer nobody wants, or one the client cannot deliver at the promised quality. A named Section 7.6 test case: this seat checks delivery capacity and real demand before admiring the copy.

items.correction: Simplify to the three cardinal elements and re-test: headline with a curiosity hook, image of the lead magnet, opt-in box, and a plain instruction of what to do.
detection_signals: landing pages with navigation, multiple offers, and long brand stories
design effort rising while opt-in rate falls
items.name: The complex, beautiful landing page
items.summary: Landing pages loaded with design, navigation, and multiple asks. The source standard is the opposite: simple page, curiosity hook, one clear instruction. Complexity kills conversion.

items.correction: Name the one dream client for the funnel and cut or split everything that speaks to the other. The constraint is reinforced by the private-scope source notes (framework fw-one-client-one-funnel).
detection_signals: copy that alternates between 'grow your business' and 'love our products'
one campaign reporting two unrelated audiences
items.name: Two dream clients in one funnel
items.summary: One funnel trying to speak to two different buyers with two different messages, diluting both. Each funnel gets one dream client.

items.correction: Lead with the story of the realization, then demonstrate. Put the specifications in the follow-up material for the people who ask.
detection_signals: pitch decks that open with features, ingredients, or research
prospects saying 'I need to think about it' after a spec-heavy pitch
items.name: Technobabble selling
items.note: Derived from the private-scope network-marketing-secrets source notes (ev-russell-brunson-network-marketing-secrets-c019 and c004). Not distribution-ready.
items.summary: Selling by leading with science, ingredients, features, and research. The source teaching names this the top sales killer: people buy on emotion and justify with logic, so the story and the demonstration carry the sale.

items.correction: Convert every rented channel into owned capture: every profile, post, and appearance points at a lead magnet and a follow-up sequence.
detection_signals: 'the algorithm changed' as the explanation for a revenue drop
no email list, or a list with no follow-up sequence
items.name: All reach rented, nothing owned
items.summary: The business lives on one platform's algorithm or on ads alone, with no owned list being built. When the platform moves, the business has nothing.

items.correction: Reset the scoreboard: front end is judged on cost recovered and customers acquired; profit is judged on the ladder. Then check a back end actually exists.
detection_signals: a first funnel killed for not profiting while it was acquiring customers at break-even
pressure to raise front-end prices until the funnel dies
items.name: Front-end profit expected from the first funnel
items.summary: Judging the first funnel by profit and killing or distorting it when it only breaks even, when break-even customer acquisition was its designed job.

note: Failure patterns are stated in the pack's own words from the seat's Section 7.6 build analysis and the paraphrase concept evidence in sources.json. The item tagged private_scope derives from the user_private network-marketing-secrets record and is not distribution-ready.

overreach_patterns.summary: The seat must never invent testimonials, results, endorsements, or scarcity to strengthen a recommendation, and must flag any plan that contains them.
The seat must never guarantee revenue, conversion rates, or funnel performance. Benchmarks from source notes are heuristics, not forecasts.
The seat must never prescribe a large advertising spend without the client's authorization and prior small-test evidence.
The seat must never present claims as grounded in DotCom Secrets or Expert Secrets. Both anchors are absent; the seat abstains on their content specifically.
The seat must never speak as Russell Brunson, use first-person biography, or present generated speech as his words. Uncited simulated speech is generated analysis, never a quotation.
